citation.title: Measurement of fast ion life time using neutron diagnostics and its application to the fast ion instability at ELM suppressed KSTAR plasma by RMP
citation.authors: J.-G. Kwak, M.H. Woo, T. Rhee

topic: Estimating KSTAR fast-ion slowing-down time from He3/fission-counter neutron decay during NBI beam blanks, applied to RMP ELM-suppressed discharges with fishbone-like activity.
own_question: Can neutron-signal decay during beam blanks estimate fast-ion slowing-down time, and how does this estimate change with MHD activity and RMP amplitude?
actual_method_and_evidence: The authors compare measured neutron decay times with a textbook slowing-down formula in a few shots (#18483, #19134, #18594). They report reduced measured-to-calculated ratios in H-mode and interpret fishbones as ion-diamagnetic using orbit and frequency arguments. The study uses no CES nowcasting, no BES/ECEI estimators and no predictive validation. Beam blanks are mentioned as used for CES background subtraction.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Beam blanks are stated to be about 10 ms and are used for CES/MSE background subtraction. The paper provides no CES report cadence or arrival timing.
validation_if_relevant: None. The work is offline and case-based, with no held-out data.
forbidden_inferences: That this paper establishes CES report latency or CES label accuracy
That this paper's RMP fast-ion results inform carbon-impurity Ti nowcasting
That the beam-blank analysis is real-time or online
That the fishbone mechanism is proven, since the authors acknowledge no explicit evidence
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude. The paper is KSTAR-specific but addresses fast-ion neutron diagnostics. It could at most support a passing note that NBI beam blanks are used for CES background subtraction, and that note is unnecessary for our framing.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
